extracted.intended_audience: USPTO trademark examining attorneys and post-registration examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for evaluating whether a provided domicile address in a trademark application or post-registration maintenance filing is acceptable, how to review responses and evidence, options for applicants (including 'no fixed physical address'), and when/how to handle petitions to waive the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of addresses presumptively unacceptable as domicile addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses that do not identify an actual street address or that function as a mail-forwarding address are presumptively unacceptable as domicile addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include P.O. boxes, “care of” (c/o) addresses, commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) addresses, registered agent (RA) addresses, private mailboxes (PMB), Army Post Office (APO), Fleet Post Office (FPO), Diplomatic Post Office (DPO), Highway Contract Route (HCR/HC) addresses, virtual office and shared workspace addresses. These generally may not serve as domicile addresses because they do not identify the location of the person’s principal home (natural person) or the juristic entity’s headquarters where senior executives direct and control activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited exceptions for certain P.O. box uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Some P.O. box addresses are acceptable despite the general presumption against P.O. boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A P.O. box address is acceptable for U.S. government entities and federally recognized American Indian and Alaska Native tribes (see TMEP §601.01(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiners must require a valid domicile address
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining attorneys and post-registration examiners are not required to confirm or research a listed domicile address in the initial application or maintenance filing, but they must require the applicant or registrant to provide an acceptable domicile address if: (1) it is apparent that the address is an unacceptable type of domicile address; or (2) the examining attorney receives specific guidance that the domicile address is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either trigger is present, issue a domicile address requirement. Do not obtain domicile address by examiner’s amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining domicile address by examiner’s amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Domicile address may not be obtained by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining attorneys may no longer obtain and enter an applicant’s domicile address by examiner’s amendment, even if the applicant indicates understanding that such information will be public. This avoids inadvertent public disclosure and ensures applicants provide domiciles themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign applicants/registrants with U.S. street addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated guidance for foreign citizens/entities that list a U.S. street address but are not represented by a qualified U.S. attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examining attorneys and post-registration examiners will not question an otherwise acceptable U.S. street address of a foreign citizen or entity provided in an application or post-registration maintenance filing unless they receive specific guidance that the address is unacceptable. Prior requirements to appoint U.S. counsel or provide supporting documentation may be withdrawn if inconsistent with this guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for evaluating a new domicile address provided in response
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to follow when an applicant/registrant provides a new domicile address in response to a domicile address requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: If it is apparent the new address is an unacceptable type or is foreign, proceed to Step 3. Step 2: If not apparent/unforeign, conduct an internet search of the new domicile address to determine acceptability based on entity type (assist from Trademark Law Library allowed). Upload a Note to the File after completing the search. Step 3: Take action based on whether the address is acceptable (accept and raise any new issues), unacceptable with no supporting arguments (maintain/make final requirement), or unacceptable with arguments/evidence (proceed to Part IV). Examiners are not required to search foreign addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and documentation requirement for address evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner conducts an internet search of a newly provided domicile address, certain documentation actions are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After completing a search, examining attorneys must upload a Note to the File indicating they conducted a search. Post-registration examiners will similarly enter a Note to the File after search completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for formal written response when asserting domicile status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any assertion that an address is the applicant’s or registrant’s principal place of business (juristic) or principal home (natural) must be made in a formal written response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in rare cases may an otherwise unacceptable address be accepted based on arguments. If uncertain, examining attorneys should consult their managing or senior attorney; post-registration examiners should consult their lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: "No fixed physical address" explanation is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed explanation that the applicant or registrant has "no fixed physical address" is no longer considered sufficient to satisfy the domicile address requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this effectively requests a waiver of the rule, the appropriate mechanism is a petition to the Director. Such a statement in lieu of providing an acceptable domicile address requires issuance and maintenance/making final of the domicile address requirement unless a petition is filed and handled per Part V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling 'no fixed physical address' in initial or pending filings
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle filings where the applicant/registrant asserts 'no fixed physical address' before publication/acceptance or in initial submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assertion appears in initial application or maintenance filing and an unacceptable type of domicile address was provided, issue and maintain the domicile address requirement. If applicant was previously advised they could provide a detailed explanation and fails to respond, make the requirement final if the application is otherwise in condition for final action. If they respond with a detailed explanation, issue a new non-final action stating that the explanation does not satisfy the requirement and inform them of response options; continued argumentative-only responses may result in making the requirement final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling 'no fixed physical address' in already approved/accepted filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment when a 'no fixed physical address' explanation was accepted before this guidance or before publication/acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to withdraw applications from publication or rescind acceptance/acknowledgment of maintenance filings that were approved/accepted prior to this guidance. However, companion applications or filings not yet approved/accepted must be evaluated under current guidance and cannot rely on acceptance in a published/accepted companion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response options for individuals asserting 'no fixed physical address'
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible ways an individual applicant/registrant who claims no fixed physical address may satisfy the domicile requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may later provide an acceptable domicile address in the Domicile Address field of a response form (for example, once they obtain a permanent legal residence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response options for juristic entities asserting 'no fixed physical address'
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible responses for a juristic applicant/registrant that claims it has no fixed physical address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A juristic entity may (1) provide a new acceptable domicile address (e.g., obtained principal place of business) or (2) provide the full name, title, and acceptable domicile address of an individual with legal authority to bind the entity (e.g., an officer or partner). The name/title/address may be included in the Domicile Address field so the domicile address is masked from public view; only information in that field is masked. Examiners may presume the person directs and controls the entity if the title clearly indicates legal authority to bind the entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option and limits of filing a petition to waive the domicile address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/registrants may petition the Director to waive the domicile address requirement based on an extraordinary situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition is an alternative but is not considered a response to an Office action; the applicant must still file a timely response to avoid abandonment. A single petition can cover multiple pending applications/registrations with pending maintenance filings. Petition content requirements are given in Part V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reviewing provided name/title/address of a binding individual
rubrics_metrics.description: How to evaluate when a juristic entity provides the name, title, and domicile address of an individual with authority to bind the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search the new address to determine acceptability. If the juristic applicant/registrant provides an individual's address but omits full name and/or title, or provides a title that does not clearly indicate legal authority to bind (e.g., 'manager' for a corporation), maintain the domicile address requirement or make it final as appropriate. Also raise any other issues resulting from the new domicile address (e.g., foreign domiciles may trigger U.S. counsel requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting masked/hidden information in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for Office actions when domicile information was provided in the hidden 'Domicile Address' field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Office action questions the domicile address or name/title and the applicant provided this information in the hidden field, the examiner must not list the address or name in the Office action. The examiner may reference the title only if the title indicates the individual does not have legal authority to bind the applicant or registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence in the form of documentation is not dispositive for unacceptable address types
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain documentation (e.g., annual reports) that identify a business address as a P.O. box or RA address does not establish that the address is the applicant’s or registrant’s domicile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some states permit registered agent addresses or P.O. boxes to be listed as business addresses without verifying they are the entity’s actual principal place of business; examiners must not accept such documentation as satisfying a domicile address requirement when the address is an unacceptable type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and requirements of a petition to waive the domicile address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: What a petition to the Director must include to seek waiver under Trademark Rule 2.189.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must include a verified statement of facts explaining lack of a fixed physical address for permanent legal residence (individual) or principal place of business (juristic). The applicant/registrant must still provide the state (or foreign equivalent) and country of their domicile (if individual), or the state and country of the domicile of the person with legal authority to bind the entity, to determine whether U.S. counsel is required. See Part V and applicable CFR/TMEP citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking the record for an existing or granted petition before issuing/maintaining requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must verify whether a petition to waive the domicile address requirement has been filed or granted prior to issuing or maintaining a requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition and any notice of pending petitions will be uploaded into all referenced records; the final petition decision will also be uploaded. If a petition has been granted, a domicile address requirement must not subsequently issue. If an applicant asserts a petition was filed or granted but no record exists, contact the Petitions Office to inquire.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to suspend an application or hold a post-registration filing for a pending petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on suspending or holding applications/filings when a petition to waive the domicile address requirement is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition is pending prior to issuing a first Office action and the application is otherwise in condition for publication (domicile address is only issue), the examiner must suspend the application pending petition decision and may not approve for publication (permission from Petitions Office not required). If a petition is pending prior to issuing a final Office action and the application is otherwise in condition for final action, the examiner may suspend only if (1) applicant requested suspension and (2) Petitions Office provided permission; use the 'Request to Suspend Action Pending Petition Decision.' The mere filing of a petition is not a response to an outstanding Office action; applicants must still respond timely to avoid abandonment. For post-registration filings, hold action pending petition decision; once decision issues, Petitions Office will notify appropriate staff. If petition pending after issuing a final action and the application is otherwise in condition for publication, the examiner may suspend pending petition decision (permission not required).
